To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an FPGA-based accelerator for the triple-DES algorithm can be used to improve the performance of the FreeS/WAN software library by 30% for the TCP protocol.
a hardware accelerated FreeS/WAN is able to achieve a 30% improvement in performance over the software version of FreeS/Wan.
an FPGA-based triple-DES accelerator is able to speedup the FreeS/WAN IPSec by 30% and the throughput is increased from 30 to 120 Mb/s.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and performance evaluation of an FPGA based triple-DES engine for FreeS/WAN.
the design of a high performance IPSec implementation and the performance of the IPSec implementation on a reconfigurale computing platform.
the implementation of an FPGA based IPSec accelerator for FreeS/WAN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an FPGA-based hardware accelerator can be used to improve the performance of IPSec by a factor of 1.3-1.5.
the FPGA accelerator has the potential to significantly increase the performance of FreeSWAN, and thus the performance of the whole VPN system.
a FPGA based accelerator can be a viable option to improve the performance of FreeSWAN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully implemented an FPGA accelerator to improve the performance of the FreeS/WAN software library and thus the performance of VPNs based on IPSec.
the performance of the FPGAaccelerated VPN system is 2.5 times of that of a software-only VPN system.
we have implemented an FPGA based accelerator to speed up the performance of Free-S/WAN and have shown a significant improvement in its performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small, inexpensive FPGA can provide a substantial speedup for a software library, even if the library itself is already highly optimized.
FPGA-based acceleration of IPSec can improve the performance of VPNs by a factor of 3.
the FPGA can be an effective platform for accelerating security algorithms.
